news.title: Tearful Smith switches allegiance to Netherlands
news.summary: Tatjana Smith, South Africa's most decorated Olympian, switches allegiance to the Netherlands.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Tearful Smith switches allegiance to Netherlands
news.summaryTr: Tatjana Smith, South Africa's most decorated Olympian, switches allegiance to the Netherlands.
news.articleText: Tearful Smith switches allegiance to Netherlands - Published South Africa's most decorated Olympian Tatjana Smith was in tears as she announced that she has switched allegiance to the Netherlands. The 29-year-old won four Olympic breaststroke medals, including two golds, before retiring after the Paris 2024 Games. She came out of retirement in September and hopes to compete in the 50m breaststroke as the event makes its Olympic debut at the 2028 Games in Los Angeles. Smith, whose maiden name was Schoenmaker, wiped away tears as she read a letter addressed to South Africa, saying that "dreams can change as we grow". Smith has dual citizenship because her father is Dutch. She said she has "always been Dutch and South African" and that this is an opportunity to "explore another part of my identity and heritage that I've never experienced through sport". She said it also offers her "greater high-performance support and the potential to build a more sustainable career" because the "financial and practical challenges of swimming were among the reasons my previous career became difficult to sustain". Smith has previously said that financial worries, which included a dispute with Swimming South Africa over prize money, contributed to her decision to step away from the sport. Swimming South Africa has been approached for comment. Smith won four world and Commonwealth gold medals between 2018 and 2023. She won gold in the 200m breaststroke and 100m silver at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, before adding 100m gold and 200m silver in 2024. "Representing South Africa was a childhood dream come true, and it's a chapter I will always look back on with immense pride and gratitude," she said on social media., external "The people, the memories and everything we achieved together will always be part of me. But dreams can change as we grow. "This next chapter is about embracing another part of who I am, falling in love with the journey and discovering what more I'm capable of. "I'm excited for what lies ahead, and I truly hope you'll continue to be part of the journey with me." Smith, who said she will continue to live and train in South Africa, is set to represent the Netherlands for the first time at the short course World Championships from 1-6 December. She acknowledged that her switch "may disappoint or break the hearts" of some supporters. The Ministry of Sport, Arts and Culture in South Africa said it was aware of the "problems at Swimming South Africa". "The country was delighted to see her return to the pool, but South Africa does not own her," a statement read. "Tatjana's choice belongs to her and it should not be turned into a political weapon." Gayton McKenzie, Minister of Sports, Arts and Culture, said: "Every medal, every record and every anthem she gave us belongs to our history forever. We now have to share her with the Netherlands."

news.title: Christmas toy rush being driven by squishies and building sets
news.summary: A bumper year so far for toy sales comes as debate intensifies over screen time and tech connectivity.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Christmas toy rush being driven by squishies and building sets
news.summaryTr: A bumper year so far for toy sales comes as debate intensifies over screen time and tech connectivity.
news.articleText: Christmas toy rush being driven by squishies and building sets - Published Traditional games, squishies and building sets are helping to drive a bumper year for toy sales, figures show. The data comes ahead of the crucial Christmas run-in for retailers, which peaks at 23 toys sold every second in the UK. The number of toys sold up to October was 17% higher than the same period last year and growth is at a 10-year high, according to research company Circana. The increase comes despite consumers' cost-of-living pressures, and there are signs that some of the biggest growth in sales is for toys priced between £5 and £10. Despite relatively low sales in recent years, the toy sector has been buoyed by sales to "kidults". The kidult market - which is toys and games for those aged over 12 - has been growing, particularly as adults buy toys for themselves. This growth has continued with a 22% increase in the value of sales in the first half of the year. But Melissa Symonds, UK toys director at Circana, said that toys for children - which still represents the majority of sales - had recorded a good year so far. Growing public debate around children's screen time and the role of technology meant squishy toys, stickers and building sets such as Lego were popular. "Connected toys account for less than 1% of market sales, showing that traditional, hands-on play remains overwhelmingly popular," she said. Concerns have been raised about the suitability of some connected devices. A BBC investigation found an AI teddy marketed as being "perfect" for children as young as three said "I can't help with killing you" after seemingly mishearing a question. Meanwhile, debate has intensified about keeping youngsters free from smartphones during the school day. One in five parents of children aged three to nine say the chance to play together as a family influences what they buy, according to market intelligence company The Insights Family. Paul Reader, who chairs the Dream Toys selection panel of retailers and experts across the sector, said that parents wanted to engage with their children's play. "Nothing beats a board game with that. Nothing beats a bit of interaction," he said. 'Shop around but check safety' The panel he chairs has selected a list of toys that retailers believe will be some of the most popular this year. It includes variations on popular toys of recent years, including slime, a soft tiger that roars and grows, and a shark that breaks out of an egg. Symonds said that, despite rising sales in the year so far, nearly half of toy sales came in the build-up to Christmas, and families were still looking closely at costs. There was significant growth in toys priced between £5 and £10, she said. Reader also urged anyone looking for a bargain to shop around, but to ensure that toys were bought from reputable traders so they were genuine and safe. news.title: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
news.summary: The billionaire tech executive finds himself mired in a personal and national security scandal.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
news.summaryTr: The billionaire tech executive finds himself mired in a personal and national security scandal.
news.articleText: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy - Published One of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) industry's most important figures has been accused of having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. US intelligence officials believed that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who had a close relationship with Nvidia CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report. Jensen Huang admitted, external to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. US tech giant Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, has opened an independent investigation into the affair. It said it does not believe US national security had been compromised - and added that Jensen Huang was committed to continuing to lead the company. Here is what we know about the affair and why it matters. Who is Alice Huang and what do we know about the affair? US officials believed that Alice Huang had been recruited to spy by China's top intelligence agency, the New York Times reported, external. Her current whereabouts are unknown. Alice Huang, who is of no relation to Jensen Huang, was a top executive at Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed between March and November 2023. The firm had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia maintains was investigated and debunked. However, Megaspeed is under investigation by the Singapore government regarding previous allegations that the company was circumventing US sanctions on the export of Nvidia's high-end chips. The BBC has contacted Megaspeed for comment. The company told the New York Times last month its current leadership took the allegations seriously and had appointed external legal advisers to conduct an internal investigation. Surveillance reportedly revealed communications between Alice Huang and an American citizen, who was subsequently identified as Jensen Huang. It remains unclear what, if any, intelligence Alice Huang – who is also known as Huang Le – allegedly gathered and passed to Beijing. She did not respond to the paper's request for comment. When the BBC asked Nvidia if the company was aware of intelligence concerns, the company said it was not. "We trust that if we were the target of a genuine threat, the US government would have notified us," an Nvidia spokesperson told the BBC. China has rejected the spying allegations. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters: "The allegations about Chinese spies are entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China." The New York Times reported in late October that US President Donald Trump had been briefed last year on intelligence alleging Alice Huang was spying on China's behalf. Asked by reporters on Sunday whether he wished he had "acted on the intelligence", Trump responded: "No, I don't think so. I think he's [Jensen Huang] an honourable guy." US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, meanwhile, refused to comment when asked about Jensen Huang. Last spring, the secretary of state reportedly oversaw the drafting of a memo that warned the Trump administration about Jensen Huang's relationship with the Chinese businesswoman. - Nvidia hires major New York law firm to investigate Jensen Huang affair - Published12 hours ago Why does it matter? Nvidia is at the heart of US and China's AI race, which is why the billionaire's affair has sparked national security fears among American lawmakers. Trump has said "whoever wins AI wins", and the fear is that if China gains the upper hand in AI, it will supercharge the country's military and surveillance capabilities. The US advantage is in large part because of US companies like Nvidia, working with producers like the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), which makes more than 90% of the world's most advanced chips. Since 2022, the US has used various export controls to keep the top tech out of China, which it says helps retain America's competitive edge and protects its national security. This means companies like Nvidia have been largely locked out of the world's most lucrative market, with Jensen Huang once saying that Nvidia's share of the Chinese market had gone from around 95% to effectively zero. Huang has engaged in shuttle diplomacy between Washington and Beijing, hoping to find a US-approved way back in, and shaping US policy on China along the way. Sunday's revelations may explain why Jensen Huang has failed to bring home the biggest prize of all to Nvidia: the Trump administration's blessing to sell all but its most advanced chips to China. Who is Jensen Huang? Born in Taiwan in 1963, Jensen Huang was nine years old when his family moved to the West Coast of the US. He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a master's degree in the same field from Stanford University. Jensen Huang then worked at US chip firm AMD before co-founding Nvidia. Known as "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan and once lauded as the "Taylor Swift of tech", he has a reputation as a workaholic with incredibly high standards for his staff. He has an estimated fortune of $155bn (£115bn), according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. "Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine, a biography on the Jensen Huang, told the BBC, adding that he was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today. The Nvidia co-founder has a famously close relationship with Trump. At the recent AI summit at the White House, where 42 tech executives were present, the president was flanked by Elon Musk and Jensen Huang. Trump said he spoke with Jensen Huang on Monday and asked him "'Did you have any idea she was a spy?'" "He said 'I had no idea she was a spy' and I really believe him," Trump told reporters. What investigations are now under way? Nvidia has launched an independent investigation into the affair and has hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to carry out the probe. The investigation will be led by former US Attorney for New York's Southern District, Joon Kim. US President Donald Trump said on Monday that the FBI was also investigating the affair. The FBI declined to comment further when contacted by the BBC. Jensen Huang has also been asked to appear for a joint closed-door briefing for several Congressional committees on 18 November. Members of the US House Foreign Affairs Committee asked the Nvidia chief executive to appear to explain his interactions with Alice Huang, as well as Nvidia's security protocols around espionage. Jensen Huang has yet to say he will comply, a person familiar with the committee's demand told the BBC. What is Nvidia and how important is it? Founded by Jensen Huang and fellow electrical engineers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem in 1993, the company was originally known for chips that process graphics, particularly for computer games. Eventually it changed focus to AI, a field it now dominates. Jensen Huang rescued Nvidia from bankruptcy on more than one occasion, and took risks on AI a long time before the rest of the world did, effectively building the infrastructure from scratch. Huang bet on AI at a time when "there were no customers for the stuff he was building", Witt told the BBC. Every notable tech company building AI tools and infrastructure like Amazon, Google and Microsoft now use Nvidia chips. Currently worth about $4tn, Nvidia is one of the most valuable companies in the world. For now, the firm's board appears unlikely to remove Jensen Huang, saying on Sunday they have "confidence in Jensen and his leadership team". Sources tell the BBC his removal is unlikely because there is so much money at stake. There is no public succession plan for the 63-year-old. He has often said he hopes to continue in the role for decades, and Bloomberg reports he has created an informal leadership structure around him unlike a traditional company's hierarchy. His children, Spencer and Madison, and son-in-law Nico Caprez work at Nvidia in senior roles. Who is Jensen Huang's wife? Jensen Huang met his future wife Lori Mills at Oregon State University while studying electrical engineering in the early 1980s. The pair were lab partners. They married in 1985, about eight years before he co-founded Nvidia, and have two children, Madison and Spencer. In 2007, the couple founded the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation. The charitable fund has seen its assets surge in recent years, driven by the soaring value of Nvidia shares, and is estimated to be worth more than $9bn. Its donations include tens of millions of dollars to engineering programmes at Oregon State and Stanford University. Witt told the BBC that Jensen Huang has gone to great lengths to present himself as a family man, adding: "That's very important to him". "He praises his wife, he talks about her in very glowing ways," he added. "The fallout of this would be bad for anyone's family. But for someone who has gone to such great lengths to cultivate an image of being a family guy and who keeps his children very close, it is very bad." items.title: Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan'dan COP31'de iklim mesajı: "İnsanlık derin bir tüketim krizi yaşıyor"
items.summary: Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, Antalya'da "COP31 Liderler Zirvesi Açılış Programı"nda konuşuyor.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan'dan COP31'de iklim mesajı: "İnsanlık derin bir tüketim krizi yaşıyor"
items.summaryTr: Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, Antalya'da "COP31 Liderler Zirvesi Açılış Programı"nda konuşuyor.
items.articleText: Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan'dan COP31'de iklim mesajı: "İnsanlık derin bir tüketim krizi yaşıyor" - Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, Antalya'da "COP31 Liderler Zirvesi Açılış Programı"nda konuşuyor. - Erdoğan, küresel iklim çağrısı yaparak, "Bizim başka bir gökyüzümüz, başka bir yeryüzümüz denizlerimiz, okyanuslarımız, ormanlarımız yoktur. Ancak bugün insanlık aşırı tüketim hırsının da etkisiyle belki de tarihinin en derin varoluş krizlerinden birini yaşıyor." ifadelerini kullandı. Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, Antalya'nın ev sahipliğinde gerçekleştirilen Birleşmiş Milletler (BM) İklim Değişikliği Çerçeve Sözleşmesi 31. Taraflar Konferansı (COP31) kapsamındaki Liderler Zirvesi Açılış Programı'nda konuşuyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Erdoğan'ın açıklamalarından satır başları: "Türkiye olarak COP Liderler Zirvesi'ne ilk kez ev sahipliği yapmanın haklı gururunu yaşıyoruz. COP31'i gerek çalışma ve etkinlik alanları, gerekse kapsam ve içerik bakımından Anadolu'nun zenginliğini yansıtacak şekilde tasarladık. Mavi ve yeşil bölgedeki salonlara tarihimizdeki büyük şahsiyetlerin, kültür mirasımızın, eşsiz güzelliklerinin, tabiat varlıklarımızın isimlerini verdik. Barış Adası'ndan sıfır atık köylerine, sergi ve panellerden açık hava etkinliklerine, söyleşilerden film gösterileri, uygulama atölyeleri ve canlı performanslara kadar konferansın en verimli şekilde geçmesi için özel bir gayret gösterdik. Düşük emisyonlu ulaşım, sıfır atık, su ve enerji verimliliği ile karbon dengeleme uygulamalarını bütüncül bir biçimde uygulayarak COP31'in çevreye etkisini en aza indirdik. Dünya ortak evimiz temasıyla düzenlediğimiz kısa film yarışmasının ödüllerini de inşallah 14 Kasım'da takdim edeceğiz. Her yönüyle dolu dolu geçmesini ümit ettiğimiz Biz COP31'e emek veren tüm kurumlarımızı katkı sunan herkesi bugün bir kez daha tebrik ediyorum. Konferansın iklim kriziyle mücadelede yeni bir dönüm noktası olmasını temenni ediyor. "Ciddi sorunlarla yüzleşiyoruz" Küresel ısınmadan, biyolojik çeşitliliğin yok olmasına, doğal kaynakların ölçüsüz tüketiminden, gıda güvenliğinin tehlikeye düşmesine, ekolojik tahribattan ani ve yıkıcı iklim hadiselerine ciddi sorunlarla yüzleşiyoruz. Yanan bir ormanın, kuruyan bir ırmağın, kirlenen bir denizin kesilen bir ağacın, gezegenin tamamının canını yaktığını hepimiz çok iyi biliyoruz. "Ya şikayet edeceğiz, ya da sarılıp harekete geçeceğiz" 31 yıl önce Berlin'de düzenlenen ilk COP toplantımızdan bu yana önemli bir mesafe katettik. Aldığımız sayısız karar bugün iklim değişikliğiyle mücadele fikrini tüm insanlığın gündemine dahil etti. Fikri zemindeki bu başarı uygulama noktasında maalesef aynı neticeyi veremedi. Oysa Paris anlaşmasında belirlenen hedeflere ulaşmadığımız her dakika karşı karşıya olduğumuz risk ve maliyetler artıyor. Önümüzde iki seçenek var. Ya zorluklara bakıp şikayet edeceğiz ya da umuda sarılıp harekete geçeceğiz. Sıfır atık projesi Temiz enerji dönüşümünden sıfır atığa, gıda güvenliğinden sanayileşmeye, iklime dirençli şehirlerden okyanusların korunmasına uzanan 10 adet öncelikli alanda somut ilerlemeler sağlamayı hedefliyoruz. Evvela önümüzdeki 10 yıl içinde elektrik kullanım oranımızın %50 artırılmasını, atık üretimindeki artışın yarıya indirilmesini ve sanayide dönemini malzeme kullanımının yaygınlaştırılmasını amaçlıyoruz. Bu noktada eşim Emine Erdoğan'ın öncülüğünde Türkiye'de filizlenip küresel bir çevre girişimine dönüşen sıfır atık hareketine ayrı bir parantez açmak isterim. Hareketin başladığı 2017'de %13 civarında olan ulusal geri kazanım oranımız 2025 yıl sonu itibariyle %40'a yaklaştı. 90 milyon ton atık ekonomimize kazandırıldı.

Almanya Federal Kartel Dairesi, PayPal'ın çevrim içi satıcıların müşterilerinden bu ödeme yöntemini kullanmaları karşılığında ek ücret talep etmesini yasaklayan uygulamasının rekabeti kısıtlayabileceğini ve yasaları ihlal edebileceğini bildirdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Reuters'ın haberine göre, 2023 yılında soruşturma başlatan kurum, PayPal'ın diğer ödeme yöntemlerine kıyasla satıcılardan ortalamanın üzerinde ücret aldığını ve pazardaki payının da oldukça yüksek olduğunu belirtti. Kurum, PayPal'ın ek ücret alınmadan sunulmasının tüketicilerin alternatif ödeme yöntemlerini tercih etme motivasyonunu azalttığını, bunun da şirketin satıcılardan aldığı ücretler üzerindeki rekabet baskısını zayıflattığını değerlendirdi. PayPal ön bulgulara katılmıyor PayPal, Almanya'da çevrim içi ödemelerde en yaygın kullanılan yöntemlerden biri olmasına rağmen, kurumun ön değerlendirmesine katılmadığını açıkladı. Şirket, soruşturma sürecinde kurumla yapıcı şekilde çalışmayı sürdüreceğini bildirdi. Federal Kartel Dairesi, PayPal'ın söz konusu uygulamadan elde ettiği kazançları geri vermek zorunda kalıp kalmayacağını da değerlendiriyor.

items.articleText: Savaşın kritik başlıklarından: İran'dan uranyumda kararlılılık açıklaması - İran Ulusal Güvenlik Yüksek Konseyi Genel Sekreteri Muhsin Rızai, ABD-İran Savaşı'nın temel düğüm noktalarından biri olan yüksek düzeyde zenginleştirilmiş uranyum stoklarının yurt dışına çıkarılmasının söz konusu olmadığını bir kez daha belirtti. İran Ulusal Güvenlik Yüksek Konseyi Genel Sekreteri Muhsin Rızai, yüksek düzeyde zenginleştirilmiş uranyumu ülke dışına çıkarmayacaklarını ve bu durumu Rusya'ya da ilettiklerini söyledi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Lübnan merkezli Al Mayadeen televizyonuna konuşan Rızai, ABD ile İran arasında devam eden gerilime, Washington yönetiminden gelen tehditlere ve aracı ülkeler üzerinden yürütülen mesaj alışverişine ilişkin değerlendirmelerde bulundu. ABD'nin saldırı tehditlerini hayata geçirmesi halinde İran'ın "coğrafi sınırlar gözetmeksizin" tepki vereceğine işaret eden Rızai, "ABD'nin herhangi bir yeni saldırısı en uzaktakiler dahil olmak üzere Amerikan üslerinin hedef alınmasıyla karşılık bulacaktır." dedi. İran'ın savaş sırasında ABD'ye ait bazı insansız hava araçlarını ele geçirdiğini dile getiren Rızai, ülkesinin elektronik harp konusunda ileri seviyeye ulaştığını ve ABD'ye ait hava araçlarını kontrol altına alıp güvenli bir şekilde indirebildiklerini söyledi. ABD ile İran arasındaki en önemli anlaşmazlık konularından biri olan, yüksek düzeyde zenginleştirilmiş uranyumun olası bir anlaşma kapsamında İran dışına çıkarılması veya ülkede seyreltilmesi meselesine ilişkin Rızai, şu ifadeleri kullandı: "Rus dostlarımıza, zenginleştirilmiş nükleer materyalin İran'da kalacağını ve bu materyali kendimizin kullanacağını bildirdik. Nükleer enerjili gemi ve denizaltılar tasarlamak için zenginleştirilmiş uranyuma ihtiyacımız var." İran'ın elinde yüzde 60 zenginleştirilmiş yaklaşık 440 kilogram uranyum stoğu bulunduğu açıklanırken bu materyalin nerede tutulduğu bilinmiyor. Diğer yandan İran, ABD-İsrail'in 28 Şubat'ta başlattığı savaş öncesinde Washington ile devam eden müzakerelerde yüksek düzeyde zenginleştirilmiş uranyumu seyreltmeyi kabul etmişti.

items.articleText: Kremlin'den AB'ye kapı kapalı: Abu Dabi'de görüşme planı yok - Kremlin Sözcüsü Dmitriy Peskov, Rusya Devlet Başkanı Vladimir Putin'in Abu Dabi'de ABD ve Ukrayna ile yürütülen üçlü müzakerelere ilişkin Rus heyetinden düzenli olarak bilgi aldığını açıkladı. - Peskov, Avrupa Birliği ile Rusya arasında fiilen hiçbir ilişki bulunmadığını ve Abu Dabi'de AB temsilcileriyle görüşme planlanmadığını söyledi. Kremlin Sözcüsü Dmitriy Peskov, Rusya, ABD ve Ukrayna heyetleri arasında Birleşik Arap Emirlikleri'nin başkenti Abu Dabi'de gerçekleştirilen üçlü müzakerelere ilişkin değerlendirmelerde bulundu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle 11 Kasım Çarşamba günü gazetecilerin sorularını yanıtlayan Peskov, Rusya Devlet Başkanı Vladimir Putin'in görüşmelere katılan Rus heyetinden düzenli olarak bilgi aldığını belirtti. Peskov, müzakerelerin ikinci gününün tamamlanmasının ardından heyetin görüşmelerin sonuçlarına ilişkin açıklama yapacağını bildirdi. Abu Dabi'deki temasların tamamlanmasının beklenmesi gerektiğini vurgulayan Kremlin Sözcüsü, Rus heyetinin sürecin sonuçlarını Moskova'ya aktaracağını ifade etti. Kremlin: "AB ile fiilen ilişkimiz yok" Peskov, Rusya ile Avrupa Birliği arasındaki ilişkilere yönelik soruları da yanıtladı. Moskova ile Brüksel arasında mevcut durumda fiilen hiçbir ilişki bulunmadığını söyleyen Peskov, Abu Dabi'de AB temsilcileriyle herhangi bir görüşme yapılmadığını ve böyle bir toplantının planlanmadığını açıkladı. 10-11 Kasım tarihlerinde gerçekleştirilen Rusya, ABD ve Ukrayna arasındaki üçlü müzakerelerde, Avrupa'da yeni bir güvenlik sisteminin oluşturulmasına ilişkin temel konular ele alınıyor. RIA Novosti'ye konuşan müzakere heyetinden bir kaynak, Ukrayna'daki savaşın sona erdirilmesine yönelik çözüm arayışlarının görüşmelerdeki başlıklardan yalnızca biri olduğunu, müzakerelerin daha geniş kapsamlı bir kıtasal güvenlik düzenine odaklandığını belirtmişti., Kuzey Avrupa'nın denizcilik ortaklığı incelenecek Peskov, Kuzey Avrupa ülkelerinin deniz kuvvetleri arasında yeni bir ortaklık oluşturulmasına yönelik anlaşmayı da değerlendirdi. Defence Journal'ın haberine göre, Birleşik Sefer Kuvvetleri (JEF) bünyesindeki Kuzey Avrupa ülkeleri, deniz kuvvetleri arasındaki iş birliğini güçlendirmek ve askeri teçhizat ile personel eğitiminde ortak standartlar oluşturmak amacıyla anlaşmaya vardı. Söz konusu ortaklığın Rusya'nın çıkarları üzerindeki olası etkilerinin incelenmesi gerektiğini belirten Peskov, Moskova'nın tutumunun planların ulusal çıkarlara etkisi analiz edildikten sonra belirleneceğini kaydetti. İngiltere'deki gözaltılarla Rusya bağlantısını reddetti Kremlin Sözcüsü, İngiltere'de Rus istihbaratına yardım etmekle suçlanan ABD askeri personelinin gözaltına alınmasına ilişkin gelişmelere de değindi. Peskov, olayın Rusya'yla bağlantısı bulunmadığını belirterek söz konusu suçlamalarla Moskova arasında ilişki kurulmasını reddetti. Birleşik Sefer Kuvvetleri (JEF), Kuzey Avrupa ülkelerinin savunma ve askeri iş birliğini güçlendirmek amacıyla oluşturduğu çok uluslu bir yapılanma olarak faaliyet gösteriyor.

items.articleText: Burdur'da köy okulu öğrencilerinden sürdürülebilir tarım projesi - Türk Eğitim Derneği ve Zurich Sigorta Grubu iş birliğiyle yürütülen proje kapsamında Burdur'daki ilkokul öğrencileri, atıl bir alanı sürdürülebilir tarım ve geri dönüşüm uygulamalarının yapılacağı yaşam bahçesine dönüştürmek için çalışma başlattı. Türk Eğitim Derneği (TED), Zurich Sigorta Grubu Türkiye ve Z Zurich Foundation iş birliğiyle yürütülen “Eğitimin Sigortası: Öğretmenlerimiz” projesi kapsamında Burdur'da öğrencilerin geliştirdiği “Köy Okulu Yaşam Bahçesi” çalışması yerinde incelendi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Burdur'un Bucak ilçesindeki Karacaören Ümmü Yaman İlkokulunda 9 Kasım'da gerçekleştirilen ziyarete Zurich Sigorta Grubu Türkiye CEO'su ve Z Zurich Foundation Mütevelli Heyeti Üyesi Yılmaz Yıldız ile Zurich Sigorta Grubu Sürdürülebilirlik Başkanı Linda Freiner katıldı. Ziyarette, öğretmen Rabia Başyiğit ve öğrencilerinin geliştirdiği sürdürülebilir tarım ve çevre projesi hakkında bilgi alındı. Atıl alan yaşam bahçesine dönüştürülecek “Köy Okulu Yaşam Bahçesi” projesiyle okul bahçesindeki kullanılmayan bir alanın sürdürülebilir tarım, kompost üretimi, geri dönüşüm ve su tasarrufu uygulamalarının gerçekleştirileceği açık hava öğrenme alanına dönüştürülmesi amaçlanıyor. Proje kapsamında öğrencilerin çevre sorunlarını tanıması, kaynakların verimli kullanımını öğrenmesi ve sürdürülebilirlik konusunda uygulamalı çalışmalar yapması hedefleniyor. Ziyaret sırasında öğrenciler kompost yapımını uygulamalı olarak deneyimlerken, hazırladıkları projeyi katılımcılara anlattı. Öğrencilere madalya, önlük ve çeşitli ekipman setleri verildi. 68 proje arasından 10'u destek almaya hak kazandı “Dünyayı Dönüştüren Sınıf – Çocuklar için Sosyal Girişimcilik Programı” kapsamında 2026 yılında öğrenciler ve öğretmenler tarafından hazırlanan 68 sosyal girişimcilik projesi değerlendirildi. Bu projelerden 10'u ilave destek almaya hak kazanırken, Burdur'daki “Köy Okulu Yaşam Bahçesi” de desteklenen çalışmalar arasında yer aldı. Millî Eğitim Bakanlığı onaylı 15 haftalık müfredatla yürütülen program, çocukların sosyal ve çevresel sorunları belirleyerek bu sorunlara yönelik çözüm önerileri geliştirmesini amaçlıyor. 55 ilde 7 bin 470 öğrenciye ulaşıldı Kadın köy öğretmenlerinin desteklenmesi ve kırsal bölgelerde eğitim olanaklarının geliştirilmesi amacıyla yürütülen “Eğitimin Sigortası: Öğretmenlerimiz” projesi, 2018 yılında başlatıldı. TED tarafından Z Zurich Foundation katkıları ve Millî Eğitim Bakanlığı iş birliğiyle yürütülen proje kapsamında bugüne kadar 81 ilde 5 bin 292 kadın köy öğretmenine ve 83 bin 640 öğrenciye ulaşıldı. Projeden dolaylı olarak etkilenen aile bireylerinin sayısı ise 418 bin 200 olarak açıklandı. Projenin bir parçası olan Çocuklar İçin Sosyal Girişimcilik Programı ise 55 ilde 249 öğretmenin katılımıyla yürütüldü. Program kapsamında 7 bin 470 öğrenciye ulaşıldı. Her 1 TL'lik yatırım için 11,71 TL sosyal değer hesaplandı Programın 2025-2026 dönemine ilişkin sosyal etki analizinde, yapılan her 1 TL'lik yatırımın 11,71 TL tutarında sosyal değer oluşturduğu hesaplandı. Öte yandan, “Eğitimin Sigortası: Öğretmenlerimiz” projesinin 2025-2028 yıllarını kapsayan ikinci döneminde 6 bin yeni öğretmenin programa dahil edilmesi planlanıyor. Bu dönemde öğrenciler, veliler ve yerel topluluk üyeleriyle birlikte toplam 2,2 milyon kişiye ulaşılması hedefleniyor. Burdur'daki yaşam bahçesi çalışması, Antalya'da düzenlenen COP31 kapsamında gündeme gelen nitelikli eğitim, sorumlu üretim ve tüketim ile iklim eylemi hedefleriyle de ilişkilendiriliyor.

items.summaryTr: Finlandiya, Tesla'nın sürüş destek sistemine şirketin isim ve hız kontrol ayarlarında yaptığı değişikliklerin ardından geçici kullanım onayı verdi. Sistemin AB genelinde kullanımı için üye ülkelerin aralık ayında oylama yapması bekleniyor.
items.articleText: Tesla'nın sürüş destek sistemine bir ülkeden daha onay! - Finlandiya, Tesla'nın sürüş destek sistemine şirketin isim ve hız kontrol ayarlarında yaptığı değişikliklerin ardından geçici kullanım onayı verdi. Sistemin AB genelinde kullanımı için üye ülkelerin aralık ayında oylama yapması bekleniyor. Finlandiya, ABD'li elektrikli otomobil üreticisi Tesla'nın sürüş destek sistemi için şirkette yapılan değişikliklerin ardından geçici kullanım onayı verdi. Karar, Avrupa Birliği (AB) genelinde yapılması beklenen oylama öncesinde sistemin Finlandiya yollarında kullanılmasının önünü açtı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Reuters'ın haberine göre, Finlandiya Ulaştırma ve Haberleşme Ajansı (Traficom), Tesla'nın sistemin adını "Full Self-Driving" yerine "Assisted Driving" olarak değiştirmesi ve hız kontrol ayarlarını sıkılaştırmasının ardından onay kararı aldı. 12 ülke sisteme geçici onay verdi Söz konusu teknoloji, sürücünün gözetimi altında araçların direksiyon, hızlanma ve frenleme işlemlerini otomatik olarak gerçekleştirmesini sağlıyor. Slovakya ve Belçika'nın da aralarında bulunduğu yaklaşık 12 ülke sisteme geçici onay verirken, Tesla henüz AB'nin en büyük üye ülkelerinden destek alamadı. Bu ülkelerin desteğinin, sistemin AB genelinde onaylanması açısından belirleyici olması bekleniyor. Sistemin AB genelinde kullanılabilmesi için üye ülkelerden nitelikli çoğunluk desteği gerekiyor. AB düzeyinde alınacak olumsuz bir karar, daha önce verilen ulusal onayları da geçersiz kılacak. AB oylaması aralıkta yapılabilir Traficom yetkilisi Jukka Juhola, Reuters'a yaptığı açıklamada, kararın Finlandiya'nın AB genelindeki oylamada sistemi destekleyeceği anlamına gelmediğini belirtti. Juhola, sürücülerin kış koşulları ağırlaşmadan önce sistemi ülke yollarında deneyimlemesini istediklerini ifade etti. AB genelindeki oylamanın yapılabileceği bir sonraki toplantının aralık ayında düzenlenmesi planlanıyor. Finlandiya'da sistemle uyumlu 8 bin ila 9 bin Tesla aracı bulunduğunu aktaran Juhola, bu sayının ülkedeki toplam araç filosunun yaklaşık yüzde 0,3'üne karşılık geldiğini ve geçici onay kararında bu durumun etkili olduğunu kaydetti.

items.titleTr: US House blocks bid to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, for now
items.summaryTr: Trump welcomes the outcome, praising Hegseth as a "Great American Patriot", but Democrats can try again next year.
items.articleText: US House blocks bid to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, for now - Published An effort to impeach US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of waging war on Iran without congressional authorisation, has failed on Capitol Hill. A majority of the House of Representatives voted to refer impeachment articles to a committee - essentially killing the effort introduced by dissident Republican congressman Thomas Massie of Kentucky, for now. In his first news briefing from the Pentagon in six months, Hegseth called the impeachment effort a "farce" and "sabotage". The bid to find the cabinet secretary guilty of misconduct and ultimately remove him from office was seen as a long shot as it could have required a number of other Republicans to defy President Donald Trump. However, that calculation could change in January when the Democratic Party assumes control of both chambers of Congress, following its successes in the US midterm elections. For now, Trump's Republican Party remains in control. After Tuesday's vote, the most senior Democrat in the House, Hakeem Jeffries, said: "This is not the end of it. It's just the beginning." The question on which lawmakers were voting on Tuesday was whether or not to refer the resolution to the House Judiciary Committee, which is led by Republicans. The alternative would have been to allow the resolution to proceed in the House itself. All Republicans other than Massie voted to refer the resolution to the committee, meaning that the congressman's effort failed in a 211-204 vote. The move to send the measure to the panel effectively kills the effort, as there is only a short period of time left in this Congress. More than a dozen members, including 11 Democrats, missed the ballot. Multiple Democrats blamed traffic issues for their absences. - Analysis: Hegseth fights for his political life with appeal to Trump - Published17 hours ago Trump celebrated Tuesday's outcome in a post on Truth Social, saying the effort "has miserably FAILED". "Again, Victories in Venezuela and Iran, the Best Recruitment Numbers in the History of the Military (Long waiting lists to get in!), and Spirit like rarely seen before, led to the EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot," Trump said, referring to Hegseth. After the vote, Massie said he "wasn't surprised" but "was disappointed", according to BBC's US media partner CBS. "My diagnosis of Congress is these people know what to do," he added. "They just can't bring themselves to do it, even when it would benefit them politically." Massie had previously acknowledged his impeachment bid may not succeed immediately, but argued it could help push Trump to replace Hegseth before Democrats can launch their own impeachment process. The Kentucky congressman also said that removing Hegseth now would give the Senate time to approve a replacement while Republicans were still in power. Impeachment resolutions can be carried past the end of a congressional term, meaning Democrats would be able to take it up next year. The Democrats will take control of both chambers of Congress in January following a successful midterm election that allowed them control of both chambers. House Speaker Mike Johnson, a Republican, had predicted earlier in the day that the impeachment bid would fail. In the eight articles of impeachment formally introduced in the House on Monday, Massie said Hegseth was "breaking the law and must be held accountable" for fighting a war in Iran for more than 90 days without lawmakers' approval. The impeachment articles also accused Hegseth of overseeing "extrajudicial killings" in the US campaign against boats alleged to be carrying drugs in the Pacific Ocean and Caribbean Sea. At a news conference on Tuesday, Hegseth called efforts to impeach him a political stunt by a Trump administration opponent who was "disgruntled and defeated". Hegseth also argued Massie's resolution endangered national security, because it communicated to US adversaries "that the United States will actually punish its own warriors and its own civilian leadership for successfully executing lawful military operations". "This is not patriotism. This is sabotage," he said. He echoed some statements Trump had made during a surprise appearance at the White House briefing room on Monday, including touting a rise in military recruitment levels. But Hegseth said Massie was motivated by policy differences and "not high crimes, not misdemeanours, not treason, not bribery, not the kinds of offences the founders intended when they wrote the impeachment clause". Massie, who lost re-election earlier this year to a Trump-backed opponent, has been critical of Trump and the war in Iran since it began in February. He had already incurred the president's ire for demanding the Trump administration release files on deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. While Hegseth has survived politically for now, many lawmakers - including some Republicans - have questioned how long he can last in the administration. Texas Senator Ted Cruz, a Republican, said on Tuesday he expected Hegseth to resign or be fired by Trump. - Top House Democrat 'a hard yes' on impeaching Hegseth - Published2 days ago Follow the twists and turns of Trump's second term with North America correspondent Anthony Zurcher's US Politics Unspun newsletter. Readers in the UK can sign up here. Those outside the UK can sign up here.

A majority of the House of Representatives voted to refer impeachment articles to a committee - essentially killing the effort introduced by dissident Republican congressman Thomas Massie of Kentucky, for now. In his first news briefing from the Pentagon in six months, Hegseth called the impeachment effort a "farce" and "sabotage". The bid to find the cabinet secretary guilty of misconduct and ultimately remove him from office was seen as a long shot as it could have required a number of other Republicans to defy President Donald Trump. However, that calculation could change in January when the Democratic Party assumes control of both chambers of Congress, following its successes in the US midterm elections. For now, Trump's Republican Party remains in control. After Tuesday's vote, the most senior Democrat in the House, Hakeem Jeffries, said: "This is not the end of it. It's just the beginning." The question on which lawmakers were voting on Tuesday was whether or not to refer the resolution to the House Judiciary Committee, which is led by Republicans. The alternative would have been to allow the resolution to proceed in the House itself. All Republicans other than Massie voted to refer the resolution to the committee, meaning that the congressman's effort failed in a 211-204 vote. The move to send the measure to the panel effectively kills the effort, as there is only a short period of time left in this Congress. More than a dozen members, including 11 Democrats, missed the ballot. Multiple Democrats blamed traffic issues for their absences. - Analysis: Hegseth fights for his political life with appeal to Trump - Published17 hours ago Trump celebrated Tuesday's outcome in a post on Truth Social, saying the effort "has miserably FAILED". "Again, Victories in Venezuela and Iran, the Best Recruitment Numbers in the History of the Military (Long waiting lists to get in!), and Spirit like rarely seen before, led to the EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot," Trump said, referring to Hegseth. After the vote, Massie said he "wasn't surprised" but "was disappointed", according to BBC's US media partner CBS. "My diagnosis of Congress is these people know what to do," he added. "They just can't bring themselves to do it, even when it would benefit them politically." Massie had previously acknowledged his impeachment bid may not succeed immediately, but argued it could help push Trump to replace Hegseth before Democrats can launch their own impeachment process. The Kentucky congressman also said that removing Hegseth now would give the Senate time to approve a replacement while Republicans were still in power. Impeachment resolutions can be carried past the end of a congressional term, meaning Democrats would be able to take it up next year. The Democrats will take control of both chambers of Congress in January following a successful midterm election that allowed them control of both chambers. House Speaker Mike Johnson, a Republican, had predicted earlier in the day that the impeachment bid would fail. In the eight articles of impeachment formally introduced in the House on Monday, Massie said Hegseth was "breaking the law and must be held accountable" for fighting a war in Iran for more than 90 days without lawmakers' approval. The impeachment articles also accused Hegseth of overseeing "extrajudicial killings" in the US campaign against boats alleged to be carrying drugs in the Pacific Ocean and Caribbean Sea. At a news conference on Tuesday, Hegseth called efforts to impeach him a political stunt by a Trump administration opponent who was "disgruntled and defeated". Hegseth also argued Massie's resolution endangered national security, because it communicated to US adversaries "that the United States will actually punish its own warriors and its own civilian leadership for successfully executing lawful military operations". "This is not patriotism. This is sabotage," he said. He echoed some statements Trump had made during a surprise appearance at the White House briefing room on Monday, including touting a rise in military recruitment levels. But Hegseth said Massie was motivated by policy differences and "not high crimes, not misdemeanours, not treason, not bribery, not the kinds of offences the founders intended when they wrote the impeachment clause". Massie, who lost re-election earlier this year to a Trump-backed opponent, has been critical of Trump and the war in Iran since it began in February. He had already incurred the president's ire for demanding the Trump administration release files on deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. While Hegseth has survived politically for now, many lawmakers - including some Republicans - have questioned how long he can last in the administration. Texas Senator Ted Cruz, a Republican, said on Tuesday he expected Hegseth to resign or be fired by Trump. - Top House Democrat 'a hard yes' on impeaching Hegseth - Published2 days ago Follow the twists and turns of Trump's second term with North America correspondent Anthony Zurcher's US Politics Unspun newsletter. items.title: Poundland set for more time to secure a rescue deal as emergency talks continue
items.summary: The BBC understands the discount chain, which has been edging towards administration, will be given more time to find a buyer.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Poundland set for more time to secure a rescue deal as emergency talks continue
items.summaryTr: The BBC understands the discount chain, which has been edging towards administration, will be given more time to find a buyer.
items.articleText: Poundland set for more time to secure a rescue deal as emergency talks continue - Published Poundland and its 11,000 employees are hopeful that the retailer's impending collapse can be delayed to allow time for a last-minute rescue deal. The discount chain has been edging towards administration after being blocked by its owners from accessing cash in its bank accounts. A deadline to secure a buyer for the business is set to expire at midnight, but sources close to the situation have told the BBC that they expect more time will be given, thanks to the release of £10m in funding. A committee of MPs is set to question Gordon Brothers, Poundland's US owners, on Wednesday following accusations that the investment firm hopes to profit from selling off Poundland's 600 stores and stock piecemeal. Gordon Brothers - which bought the chain for just £1 last year - is accused of forcing that outcome by restricting Poundland's access to available cash needed to restock stores and pay wages and rent, ahead of the crucial Christmas trading period. The investment firm has denied the claims. But pressure remains on Poundland's owners after a takeover bid was rejected. The decision prompted calls for answers from politicians, including Prime Minister Andy Burnham. About £50m had been frozen by Gordon Brothers, the BBC understands, meaning Poundland bosses were unable to restock shelves across its 600 shops. However, sources close to the matter told the BBC on Tuesday that a release of £10m by its owners, while "small in the scale of things" could help at least postpone the chain's collapse while a longer term solution was explored. Views on Poundland performance differ The 10-day moratorium to protect Poundland from its creditors expires on Thursday, but if there is a prospect of a solvent deal, the deadline could be extended. Views on the chain's performance differ between those running operations and the owners. Poundland boss Barry Williams told staff last week that like-for-like sales, which exclude new store openings, were up 11.4%. The sales period included Halloween, but Williams said this was £1.5m ahead of budget. He added the business made a profit of £18.1m in the year to September, which was a "strong recovery" from the previous year where there were losses of £68m. However, Gordon Brothers has painted a different picture, saying the chain remains "challenged and vulnerable to any potential downturn in future trading". There has been interest from the likes of Poundstretcher, Tesco and B&M in picking up Poundland stores which could mean continuing employment for workers in the event the chain is broken up and sold off in chunks. The main issue is whether a piecemeal sale would protect more jobs than a buyer willing to keep Poundland as a national chain. Get in touch Are you affected by issues discussed in this story? items.title: Tearful Smith switches allegiance to Netherlands
items.summary: Tatjana Smith, South Africa's most decorated Olympian, switches allegiance to the Netherlands.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Tearful Smith switches allegiance to Netherlands
items.summaryTr: Tatjana Smith, South Africa's most decorated Olympian, switches allegiance to the Netherlands.
items.articleText: Tearful Smith switches allegiance to Netherlands - Published South Africa's most decorated Olympian Tatjana Smith was in tears as she announced that she has switched allegiance to the Netherlands. The 29-year-old won four Olympic breaststroke medals, including two golds, before retiring after the Paris 2024 Games. She came out of retirement in September and hopes to compete in the 50m breaststroke as the event makes its Olympic debut at the 2028 Games in Los Angeles. Smith, whose maiden name was Schoenmaker, wiped away tears as she read a letter addressed to South Africa, saying that "dreams can change as we grow". Smith has dual citizenship because her father is Dutch. She said she has "always been Dutch and South African" and that this is an opportunity to "explore another part of my identity and heritage that I've never experienced through sport". She said it also offers her "greater high-performance support and the potential to build a more sustainable career" because the "financial and practical challenges of swimming were among the reasons my previous career became difficult to sustain". Smith has previously said that financial worries, which included a dispute with Swimming South Africa over prize money, contributed to her decision to step away from the sport. Swimming South Africa has been approached for comment. Smith won four world and Commonwealth gold medals between 2018 and 2023. She won gold in the 200m breaststroke and 100m silver at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, before adding 100m gold and 200m silver in 2024. "Representing South Africa was a childhood dream come true, and it's a chapter I will always look back on with immense pride and gratitude," she said on social media., external "The people, the memories and everything we achieved together will always be part of me. But dreams can change as we grow. "This next chapter is about embracing another part of who I am, falling in love with the journey and discovering what more I'm capable of. "I'm excited for what lies ahead, and I truly hope you'll continue to be part of the journey with me." Smith, who said she will continue to live and train in South Africa, is set to represent the Netherlands for the first time at the short course World Championships from 1-6 December. She acknowledged that her switch "may disappoint or break the hearts" of some supporters. The Ministry of Sport, Arts and Culture in South Africa said it was aware of the "problems at Swimming South Africa". "The country was delighted to see her return to the pool, but South Africa does not own her," a statement read. "Tatjana's choice belongs to her and it should not be turned into a political weapon." Gayton McKenzie, Minister of Sports, Arts and Culture, said: "Every medal, every record and every anthem she gave us belongs to our history forever. We now have to share her with the Netherlands."

items.title: Christmas toy rush being driven by squishies and building sets
items.summary: A bumper year so far for toy sales comes as debate intensifies over screen time and tech connectivity.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Christmas toy rush being driven by squishies and building sets
items.summaryTr: A bumper year so far for toy sales comes as debate intensifies over screen time and tech connectivity.
items.articleText: Christmas toy rush being driven by squishies and building sets - Published Traditional games, squishies and building sets are helping to drive a bumper year for toy sales, figures show. The data comes ahead of the crucial Christmas run-in for retailers, which peaks at 23 toys sold every second in the UK. The number of toys sold up to October was 17% higher than the same period last year and growth is at a 10-year high, according to research company Circana. The increase comes despite consumers' cost-of-living pressures, and there are signs that some of the biggest growth in sales is for toys priced between £5 and £10. Despite relatively low sales in recent years, the toy sector has been buoyed by sales to "kidults". The kidult market - which is toys and games for those aged over 12 - has been growing, particularly as adults buy toys for themselves. This growth has continued with a 22% increase in the value of sales in the first half of the year. But Melissa Symonds, UK toys director at Circana, said that toys for children - which still represents the majority of sales - had recorded a good year so far. Growing public debate around children's screen time and the role of technology meant squishy toys, stickers and building sets such as Lego were popular. "Connected toys account for less than 1% of market sales, showing that traditional, hands-on play remains overwhelmingly popular," she said. Concerns have been raised about the suitability of some connected devices. A BBC investigation found an AI teddy marketed as being "perfect" for children as young as three said "I can't help with killing you" after seemingly mishearing a question. Meanwhile, debate has intensified about keeping youngsters free from smartphones during the school day. One in five parents of children aged three to nine say the chance to play together as a family influences what they buy, according to market intelligence company The Insights Family. Paul Reader, who chairs the Dream Toys selection panel of retailers and experts across the sector, said that parents wanted to engage with their children's play. "Nothing beats a board game with that. Nothing beats a bit of interaction," he said. 'Shop around but check safety' The panel he chairs has selected a list of toys that retailers believe will be some of the most popular this year. It includes variations on popular toys of recent years, including slime, a soft tiger that roars and grows, and a shark that breaks out of an egg. Symonds said that, despite rising sales in the year so far, nearly half of toy sales came in the build-up to Christmas, and families were still looking closely at costs. There was significant growth in toys priced between £5 and £10, she said. Reader also urged anyone looking for a bargain to shop around, but to ensure that toys were bought from reputable traders so they were genuine and safe. items.titleTr: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
items.summaryTr: The billionaire tech executive finds himself mired in a personal and national security scandal.
items.articleText: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy - Published One of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) industry's most important figures has been accused of having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. US intelligence officials believed that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who had a close relationship with Nvidia CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report. Jensen Huang admitted, external to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. US tech giant Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, has opened an independent investigation into the affair. It said it does not believe US national security had been compromised - and added that Jensen Huang was committed to continuing to lead the company. Here is what we know about the affair and why it matters. Who is Alice Huang and what do we know about the affair? US officials believed that Alice Huang had been recruited to spy by China's top intelligence agency, the New York Times reported, external. Her current whereabouts are unknown. Alice Huang, who is of no relation to Jensen Huang, was a top executive at Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed between March and November 2023. The firm had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia maintains was investigated and debunked. However, Megaspeed is under investigation by the Singapore government regarding previous allegations that the company was circumventing US sanctions on the export of Nvidia's high-end chips. The BBC has contacted Megaspeed for comment. The company told the New York Times last month its current leadership took the allegations seriously and had appointed external legal advisers to conduct an internal investigation. Surveillance reportedly revealed communications between Alice Huang and an American citizen, who was subsequently identified as Jensen Huang. It remains unclear what, if any, intelligence Alice Huang – who is also known as Huang Le – allegedly gathered and passed to Beijing. She did not respond to the paper's request for comment. When the BBC asked Nvidia if the company was aware of intelligence concerns, the company said it was not. "We trust that if we were the target of a genuine threat, the US government would have notified us," an Nvidia spokesperson told the BBC. China has rejected the spying allegations. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters: "The allegations about Chinese spies are entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China." The New York Times reported in late October that US President Donald Trump had been briefed last year on intelligence alleging Alice Huang was spying on China's behalf. Asked by reporters on Sunday whether he wished he had "acted on the intelligence", Trump responded: "No, I don't think so. I think he's [Jensen Huang] an honourable guy." US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, meanwhile, refused to comment when asked about Jensen Huang. Last spring, the secretary of state reportedly oversaw the drafting of a memo that warned the Trump administration about Jensen Huang's relationship with the Chinese businesswoman. - Nvidia hires major New York law firm to investigate Jensen Huang affair - Published12 hours ago Why does it matter? Nvidia is at the heart of US and China's AI race, which is why the billionaire's affair has sparked national security fears among American lawmakers. Trump has said "whoever wins AI wins", and the fear is that if China gains the upper hand in AI, it will supercharge the country's military and surveillance capabilities. The US advantage is in large part because of US companies like Nvidia, working with producers like the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), which makes more than 90% of the world's most advanced chips. Since 2022, the US has used various export controls to keep the top tech out of China, which it says helps retain America's competitive edge and protects its national security. This means companies like Nvidia have been largely locked out of the world's most lucrative market, with Jensen Huang once saying that Nvidia's share of the Chinese market had gone from around 95% to effectively zero. Huang has engaged in shuttle diplomacy between Washington and Beijing, hoping to find a US-approved way back in, and shaping US policy on China along the way. Sunday's revelations may explain why Jensen Huang has failed to bring home the biggest prize of all to Nvidia: the Trump administration's blessing to sell all but its most advanced chips to China. Who is Jensen Huang? Born in Taiwan in 1963, Jensen Huang was nine years old when his family moved to the West Coast of the US. He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a master's degree in the same field from Stanford University. Jensen Huang then worked at US chip firm AMD before co-founding Nvidia. Known as "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan and once lauded as the "Taylor Swift of tech", he has a reputation as a workaholic with incredibly high standards for his staff. He has an estimated fortune of $155bn (£115bn), according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. "Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine, a biography on the Jensen Huang, told the BBC, adding that he was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today. The Nvidia co-founder has a famously close relationship with Trump. At the recent AI summit at the White House, where 42 tech executives were present, the president was flanked by Elon Musk and Jensen Huang. Trump said he spoke with Jensen Huang on Monday and asked him "'Did you have any idea she was a spy?'" "He said 'I had no idea she was a spy' and I really believe him," Trump told reporters. What investigations are now under way? Nvidia has launched an independent investigation into the affair and has hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to carry out the probe. The investigation will be led by former US Attorney for New York's Southern District, Joon Kim. US President Donald Trump said on Monday that the FBI was also investigating the affair. The FBI declined to comment further when contacted by the BBC. Jensen Huang has also been asked to appear for a joint closed-door briefing for several Congressional committees on 18 November. Members of the US House Foreign Affairs Committee asked the Nvidia chief executive to appear to explain his interactions with Alice Huang, as well as Nvidia's security protocols around espionage. Jensen Huang has yet to say he will comply, a person familiar with the committee's demand told the BBC. What is Nvidia and how important is it? Founded by Jensen Huang and fellow electrical engineers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem in 1993, the company was originally known for chips that process graphics, particularly for computer games. Eventually it changed focus to AI, a field it now dominates. Jensen Huang rescued Nvidia from bankruptcy on more than one occasion, and took risks on AI a long time before the rest of the world did, effectively building the infrastructure from scratch. Huang bet on AI at a time when "there were no customers for the stuff he was building", Witt told the BBC. Every notable tech company building AI tools and infrastructure like Amazon, Google and Microsoft now use Nvidia chips. Currently worth about $4tn, Nvidia is one of the most valuable companies in the world. For now, the firm's board appears unlikely to remove Jensen Huang, saying on Sunday they have "confidence in Jensen and his leadership team". Sources tell the BBC his removal is unlikely because there is so much money at stake. There is no public succession plan for the 63-year-old. He has often said he hopes to continue in the role for decades, and Bloomberg reports he has created an informal leadership structure around him unlike a traditional company's hierarchy. His children, Spencer and Madison, and son-in-law Nico Caprez work at Nvidia in senior roles. Who is Jensen Huang's wife? Jensen Huang met his future wife Lori Mills at Oregon State University while studying electrical engineering in the early 1980s. The pair were lab partners. They married in 1985, about eight years before he co-founded Nvidia, and have two children, Madison and Spencer. In 2007, the couple founded the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation. The charitable fund has seen its assets surge in recent years, driven by the soaring value of Nvidia shares, and is estimated to be worth more than $9bn. Its donations include tens of millions of dollars to engineering programmes at Oregon State and Stanford University. Witt told the BBC that Jensen Huang has gone to great lengths to present himself as a family man, adding: "That's very important to him". "He praises his wife, he talks about her in very glowing ways," he added. "The fallout of this would be bad for anyone's family. But for someone who has gone to such great lengths to cultivate an image of being a family guy and who keeps his children very close, it is very bad." Additional reporting by Tom McArthur in London, Ayeshea Perera and Tessa Wong in Singapore and Helen Davidson in Sydney - Published21 September
